subject: Physics
description: Newton's universal law, g, weightlessness, escape velocity, satellite motion, Kepler's laws

questions.stem: Newton's UNIVERSAL LAW of gravitation states that the force between two masses is:

options.option_text: Proportional to the sum of the two masses involved
Proportional to product of masses, inverse-square of distance
Independent of mass, dependent only on the distance
Proportional to the cube of the distance separating them

questions.explanation: F = G m₁m₂ / r². Force ∝ product of masses, INVERSELY proportional to SQUARE of distance. G = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² (universal gravitational constant; measured by Cavendish, 1798). Distractor 1 — sum, not product. Distractor 3 — false (mass matters). Distractor 4 — wrong power.

questions.stem: The acceleration due to gravity (g) at the SURFACE of the Earth is approximately:

options.option_text: 5 m/s² near the Earth's surface
9.8 m/s² near the Earth's surface
20 m/s² near the Earth's surface
1.6 m/s² near the Earth's surface

questions.explanation: g ≈ 9.8 m/s² at sea level. Varies slightly with latitude (more at poles, less at equator due to Earth's bulge + rotation), with altitude (decreases with height). Distractor 4 = MOON's gravity (1.6 m/s², ~1/6 of Earth). Mars ~3.7 m/s². Jupiter ~24.8 m/s². Sun ~274 m/s².

questions.stem: ESCAPE VELOCITY from Earth's surface is approximately:

options.option_text: 7.9 km/s, the orbital velocity at low orbit
11.2 km/s, the speed needed to leave gravity
30 km/s, Earth's orbital speed around Sun
300,000 km/s, the speed of light in vacuum

questions.explanation: ESCAPE VELOCITY = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s for Earth (~40,300 km/h). Below this, an object falls back. Above, it escapes Earth's gravity. Distractor 1 = first cosmic velocity (orbital, ~7.9 km/s for low Earth orbit). Distractor 3 = Earth's orbital velocity around Sun. Distractor 4 = speed of light.

questions.stem: An astronaut in a satellite orbiting the Earth feels WEIGHTLESS because:

options.option_text: There is no gravity acting up there in space
Both astronaut and satellite are in continuous free fall
Air pressure outside zero out the felt weight
Centrifugal force exactly cancels gravity acting

questions.explanation: FREE FALL — gravity still acts (~90% of surface g at ISS altitude!), but the satellite is in continuous free fall AROUND the Earth (orbital path = falling and missing). Astronaut + satellite fall TOGETHER, so there's no normal-force pressing on astronaut → felt as weightlessness. Distractor 1 — wrong; gravity is strong even there. Distractor 3 — vacuum; no air pressure. Distractor 4 — centrifugal force is a pseudo-force in the rotating frame; gravity is what provides centripetal force in the inertial frame.

questions.stem: A GEOSTATIONARY satellite orbits at an altitude of approximately:

options.option_text: 400 km, where the ISS roughly orbits the Earth
36,000 km above the equator with 24-hour period
100 km, the boundary of space (Karman line)
200,000 km, between Earth and Moon distance

questions.explanation: Geostationary orbit (GEO) — ~35,786 km above equator. Period 23h 56min ≈ Earth's rotation → satellite appears stationary in sky. Used for communication satellites, TV broadcasting, weather (INSAT, GSAT series). Distractor 1 = LEO (Low Earth Orbit) where ISS orbits. Distractor 3 = boundary of space, not orbital. Distractor 4 = halfway to Moon, no satellites at that orbit.

questions.stem: The value of g at the EQUATOR is slightly LESS than at the POLES because:

options.option_text: The atmosphere is thicker at the equator zone
Equator is farther from centre + Earth rotates faster there
The Sun's gravity reduces the felt g near equator
Magnetic field is stronger at the equator zone

questions.explanation: Two reasons: (1) Earth is OBLATE — equatorial radius (~6378 km) > polar radius (~6357 km), so equatorial surface is FURTHER from Earth's centre → smaller g (gravitational F ∝ 1/r²). (2) Earth ROTATES — centripetal force needed for objects on the surface comes from gravity; at equator the rotational velocity is highest → effective g (felt) is reduced more. Polar g ≈ 9.83; equatorial g ≈ 9.78 m/s². Distractors 1, 3, 4 are wrong reasons.

questions.stem: Kepler's THIRD LAW of planetary motion states that the square of the orbital period is proportional to:

options.option_text: The radius of the orbit raised to the first power
The cube of the semi-major axis of the orbit
The mass of the orbiting body's celestial size
The exponential of the orbit's eccentricity values

questions.explanation: Kepler's Third Law: T² ∝ a³ (a = semi-major axis). For Solar System: T² = a³ when T is in years and a in AU. E.g., Jupiter: a = 5.2 AU; T² = 5.2³ = 140.6; T ≈ 11.86 years (matches!). Derived from Newton's law of gravitation. First two laws: (1) planets move in ELLIPTICAL orbits with the Sun at one focus; (2) equal areas swept in equal times.
